Koalas face numerous challenges, but chlamydia is one of the gravest. In many populations, around 50 percent of the marsupials are infected, leading to issues such as infertility, blindness, and starvation. As the disease spreads through wild populations, Australia has approved a vaccine that could become an important new tool for protecting the vulnerable species.
